name: Germany
note: A doctor performs the Leichenschau under Länder law. The household, the home owner or the institution must report the death to the Standesamt by the third working day. The Standesamt records it in the Sterberegister and notifies the Meldebehörde, the statistical offices, the inheritance-tax office and the Zentrales Testamentsregister, which tells the probate court. The Meldebehörde in turn sends the death to the pension insurance data office, which passes every death to Deutsche Post's Renten Service to stop benefits, and to the Federal Central Tax Office. The family need not tell these bodies. Germany has no central population register: anyone can learn of a death only by asking the municipal registration office.

steps.title: Doctor performs the Leichenschau and issues the Todesbescheinigung (Länder law)
steps.who: A physician under the Bestattungsgesetz of each Land; who may perform it, deadlines and the form vary by Land.
steps.summary: Leichenschau and the death certificate are Länder law and not recorded here. Federal law only requires that the registrar be shown a medical certificate of death.

steps.title: Confidential cause-of-death part goes to the Länder statistical offices
steps.who: The Land body that receives the confidential part of the Totenschein (designated by Länder law) forwards causes of death to the statistical offices.
steps.summary: Causes and circumstances of death from the Totenschein reach the statistical offices of the Länder at least monthly, keyed to the death register number. Which body receives the confidential part is Länder law.

steps.title: Unnatural death or unknown body reported to the public prosecutor
steps.who: Police and municipal authorities; the Staatsanwaltschaft or Amtsgericht.
steps.trigger: Signs of an unnatural death, or a body of an unknown person.
steps.summary: Police and municipal authorities must report immediately; burial then needs the prosecutor's written permission.

steps.title: Report the death to the Standesamt by the third working day
steps.who: In order: every person who lived in the same household; the person in whose home the death occurred; anyone present or with personal knowledge. Each is liable only if those earlier in the order are absent or prevented.

deadline.text: spätestens am dritten auf den Tod folgenden Werktag

steps.summary: The death is reported orally or in writing to the Standesamt for the place of death, which records it in the Sterberegister on production of the medical certificate and civil-status documents. Failing to report on time is an administrative offence.

steps.title: Hospital or care home reports the death in writing
steps.who: The operator (Träger) of a hospital, old-age or nursing home or other institution.

deadline.text: spätestens am dritten auf den Tod folgenden Werktag

steps.summary: Institutions carry the reporting duty for deaths on their premises and are liable to a fine for late or missing reports.

steps.title: Municipality reports if no one else does; authorities report deaths under official investigation
steps.who: The Gemeindebehörde for the place of death; for deaths under official investigation, the competent authority (police/prosecutor) reports in writing.
steps.trigger: No obliged informant, or an official investigation.
steps.summary: Fallbacks that ensure every death is registered.

steps.title: Sterbeurkunde issued to family and those with a legal interest
steps.who: The deceased's spouse/partner, ancestors and descendants; others only with a legal interest (siblings: a legitimate interest).
steps.summary: Death certificates are restricted to close relatives and people who show a legal interest.

steps.title: Standesamt of death notifies the Standesamt holding the birth entry
steps.who: The registering Standesamt.
steps.summary: The birth and marriage registers are linked to the death entry; other notifications follow wherever a statute requires one.

steps.title: Standesamt notifies the Meldebehörde, which records the death in the Melderegister
steps.who: The Standesamt; the municipal Meldebehörde for the deceased's residence.
steps.summary: Every civil-status change is passed to the residents' registration authority, which stores the date and place of death. There is no single central population register; the Melderegister is kept by each municipality.

steps.title: Standesamt sends death data to the Länder statistical offices
steps.who: The Standesamt; the statistical offices of the Länder, which pass data on to Destatis for current mortality figures.

deadline.text: spätestens am dritten Arbeitstag nach Eintrag in das Sterberegister

steps.summary: Death data reach official statistics within three working days of registration for mortality monitoring.

steps.title: Standesamt reports deaths to the inheritance-tax office
steps.who: The Standesamt, to the Finanzamt responsible for inheritance tax in its district.

deadline.text: binnen zehn Tagen nach Ablauf des Monats

steps.summary: Each month the Standesamt sends death certificates (or a death list) to the inheritance-tax office.

steps.title: Standesamt notifies the Zentrales Testamentsregister
steps.who: The Standesamt; the Bundesnotarkammer as the register authority.
steps.summary: The register authority checks whether wills or succession-relevant deeds are on file.

steps.title: Testament register informs the probate court and custodians
steps.who: The Bundesnotarkammer (ZTR) to the competent Nachlassgericht and the bodies holding the deposited wills.
steps.summary: The probate court learns of the death and any registered will automatically and electronically.

steps.title: Meldebehörde sends the death to the pension insurance data office
steps.who: Meldebehörden to the Datenstelle der Rentenversicherung (DSRV).
steps.trigger: Storage of the death in the Melderegister.
steps.summary: A regular statutory transmission carries the date of death (and spouse/partner data) to stop and adjust pensions and update insured records.

steps.title: Pension data office forwards all deaths to Deutsche Post (Renten Service)
steps.who: Datenstelle der Rentenversicherung to Deutsche Post AG, which pays pensions for the statutory pension and other benefit bodies.
steps.summary: Deutsche Post uses the notices to stop current benefit payments, pay the survivor's three-month advance, and pass them on to accident insurers, agricultural social insurance, supplementary and professional pension schemes.

steps.title: Meldebehörde notifies the Federal Central Tax Office
steps.who: Meldebehörden to the Bundeszentralamt für Steuern.
steps.trigger: Storage of the death in the Melderegister.
steps.summary: The date of death is added to the tax identification number record.

steps.title: Probate courts and notaries report to the inheritance-tax office
steps.who: Courts (opened wills, Erbscheine, executor certificates) and notaries.
steps.summary: Certified copies go to the inheritance-tax office on paper (electronic transmission is excluded).

steps.title: Banks and custodians report the deceased's assets to the inheritance-tax office
steps.who: Anyone who holds or manages third-party assets in the course of business (banks, custodians).
steps.trigger: The custodian learns of the death.

deadline.text: innerhalb eines Monats, seitdem der Todesfall bekanntgeworden ist

steps.summary: Balances and claims at the date of death are reported on Muster 1 (not required below EUR 5,000). This is a duty to report to the state once the bank knows, not a route by which the bank learns.

steps.title: Insurers report payouts to someone other than the policyholder
steps.who: Insurance undertakings, including Sterbekassen.
steps.trigger: Before paying a sum or annuity to someone other than the policyholder.
steps.summary: Breaches of the ErbStG § 33 duties are tax administrative offences.

steps.title: Anyone may ask the Meldebehörde whether a person has died
steps.who: Any person or private body (banks, insurers, creditors), individually or in bulk, including by automated internet query or portal.
steps.summary: A simple register extract includes the fact of death; commercial use must be declared, and advertising and address-trading uses are barred.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Third working day (Werktag) after the death.

informantDuty.note: Household members first, then the home owner, then anyone present or informed; institutions report deaths on their premises; the municipality as fallback.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: Leichenschau and any second examination (e.g. before cremation) are Länder law and not covered by this federal file.

electronicRegistration.note: Reporting is oral or written; onward notifications from the Standesamt are electronic, but no federal electronic channel for informants was found.

governmentPropagation.note: Standesamt → Meldebehörde, statistics, inheritance-tax office and ZTR; Meldebehörde → DSRV (→ Deutsche Post Renten Service) and BZSt by regular statutory transmissions.

certificateAccess.note: Spouse/partner, ancestors, descendants; others only with a legal interest.

privateSectorVerification.note: No national death file; private bodies can obtain the fact of death through a simple (including automated) Melderegister enquiry, one municipality at a time. Banks and insurers have reporting duties to the tax office but no duty to check.

gaps: Leichenschau (who may pronounce, deadlines, the Todesbescheinigung form, second examination before cremation) is Länder law under each Bestattungsgesetz and is not covered; the pronounce step is marked unverified.
Burial/cremation permits are Länder law; federally only StPO § 159(2) (prosecutor's permission in unnatural deaths) applies.

Statutory health insurers (Krankenkassen): no federal provision read showing a direct Meldebehörde → Krankenkasse death feed; SGB X § 101a covers accident, agricultural and supplementary schemes via Deutsche Post.

Electoral roll (Wählerverzeichnis from the Melderegister under the Bundeswahlordnung), identity cards/passports and driving licences: death-specific provisions not read. 2. BMeldDÜV § 8 (KBA) covers name changes only, not deaths.
The brief's 'SGB VI § 101a' does not exist; the Deutsche Post route is SGB X § 101a, fed by SGB VI § 196(2).
1. BMeldDÜV (data exchange between Meldebehörden) not read; BMG § 33(3) covers notifying other registration authorities when a person dies.
No public notice of death required by federal law; nothing recorded for the 'public' stage.
